instructions: Listen to the audio for each part and answer the questions. Each audio plays once.

listeningScripts.title: Medical Appointment Rescheduling
listeningScripts.text: Patient: Hello, I need to reschedule my appointment with Dr. Singh. Receptionist: Of course. Can I have your patient ID? Patient: It's P-9847. My appointment is next Tuesday at 2 PM, but I have a conflict. Receptionist: Let me pull that up. Yes, I see the appointment for June 10th at 2 PM. What days and times work better for you? Patient: Ideally, early morning, like 8 or 9 AM. I work afternoons. Receptionist: Let me check the doctor's schedule. Dr. Singh has an opening on Friday, June 13th at 8:30 AM. Would that suit you? Patient: Yes, that works perfectly. Receptionist: Great. I'm canceling the Tuesday 2 PM slot and booking you for Friday, June 13th at 8:30 AM. Your appointment is for a regular checkup, is that correct? Patient: Yes, and also to discuss my recent blood work results. Receptionist: Perfect. I'll add a note that you want to review the blood work. You'll need to arrive ten minutes early to fill out any updated forms. Patient: Will Dr. Singh have my test results by then? Receptionist: Yes, they'll definitely be in her file. The lab sent them in yesterday. Is there anything else? Patient: No, that's everything. Thank you.

listeningScripts.title: Music Concert Plans
listeningScripts.text: Alex: Are you going to the concert next Saturday? Casey: Which one? There are a few shows next weekend. Alex: The indie rock festival at the waterfront. Casey: Oh yeah, I've been thinking about it. How much are tickets? Alex: They're forty dollars each. Casey: That's not too bad. Who's performing? Alex: Five bands. The headliner is The Northern Stars. Casey: Oh, I love them. What time does it start? Alex: Six PM. It should wrap up around eleven. Casey: That's pretty late. Is there parking nearby? Alex: Yeah, there's a parking lot right by the venue. It's five dollars for the whole night. Casey: That's reasonable. Should we get food there or bring our own? Alex: They have food vendors there, but it's probably expensive. Casey: Let's grab something before we go then. Alex: Good idea. Want me to buy your ticket? Casey: Yeah, that would be great. Just send me the bill.

listeningScripts.title: Travel Insurance Information Session
listeningScripts.text: Welcome to our travel insurance information session. Today, I'll explain the coverage options available through our travel agency. We offer three plans: Basic, Standard, and Premium. The Basic plan covers medical emergencies, emergency dental, and evacuation. Cost is seventy-five dollars for two weeks. The Standard plan includes everything in Basic plus trip cancellation coverage, lost luggage reimbursement up to one thousand dollars, and travel delays over twelve hours. Cost is one hundred twenty dollars for two weeks. The Premium plan is our comprehensive option. It adds accidental death coverage, zero deductible for medical claims, and upgrade to two thousand five hundred dollars for lost luggage. Premium costs two hundred twenty dollars for two weeks. All plans exclude claims related to alcohol impairment or pre-existing medical conditions not disclosed. Coverage begins on your departure date and ends upon return. Claims must be filed within ninety days of the incident. You'll receive a confirmation email with your policy documents. For claims, call our toll-free number at 1-800-555-0147. Representatives are available 24/7. Questions about coverage should be directed to our customer service team. Purchase your policy at least seven days before travel.

listeningScripts.title: New Tech Campus Opens in Calgary
listeningScripts.text: A major technology development is happening in Calgary today. TechHub Prairie, a 50,000-square-meter innovation center, officially opened its doors this morning in the downtown core. The facility cost 85 million dollars to construct and is expected to create 1,200 new jobs over the next two years. The campus features office space, research laboratories, and startup incubator units. Over 40 companies have already committed to moving in, including software firms, AI research groups, and digital marketing agencies. Mayor Jyoti Gondek attended the ribbon-cutting ceremony and called it a game-changer for Alberta's economy. The provincial government provided 15 million dollars in funding to support the project. TechHub Prairie will also host weekly networking events and offer mentorship programs for emerging entrepreneurs. Officials believe this development positions Calgary as a serious competitor in Canada's tech industry.

listeningScripts.title: Community Center Renovation Project
listeningScripts.text:
Recreation Director Karen: We're finally moving forward with the community center renovation that was approved last year. The project is budgeted at 6.8 million dollars and should take about 18 months to complete. We plan to add a new fitness center, upgrade the swimming pool, and create additional youth programming spaces. This will significantly improve our facilities.

Community Member Robert: I'm glad to see this moving forward, Karen, but I'm concerned about one thing. During the construction, the center will be partially closed. My kids attend after-school programs here, and I'm worried about where they'll go during the renovation period. Many families in our community rely on these programs for childcare.

Operations Manager Susan: That's a valid concern, Robert. We've actually planned for this. We'll maintain the community room and outdoor spaces throughout the project. We can relocate the after-school programs there during construction, though it will be more crowded. We're also negotiating with the school district to potentially use school facilities as a backup location for some activities.

Youth Program Coordinator Jason: I'm excited about the upgrades, especially the new youth spaces. But Susan, we need to be realistic about the outdoor space. We currently use it for sports and recreation. If we're moving programs there, we'll have limited room for physical activities. Could we consider using a local park for some outdoor programming during construction?

listeningScripts.title: Universal Basic Income Feasibility
listeningScripts.text: I want to discuss Universal Basic Income, or UBI, and why I believe it could work in Canada. The concept is straightforward: every citizen receives a regular, unconditional cash payment from the government. Now, I know people immediately worry about the cost, but let me address that. First, UBI could replace many existing welfare programs that are expensive to administer. The bureaucracy involved in means-testing and eligibility verification costs billions. UBI would be simpler and less wasteful. Second, the economic stimulus of putting money in people's hands is significant. When people have financial security, they spend more, which supports businesses and creates jobs. Third, UBI addresses real problems: poverty, economic instability, and lack of opportunity. We've seen pilot projects in Kenya, Finland, and Canada that show positive outcomes. In Kenya, UBI increased business formation by 32 percent. In Finland, participants reported better mental health and less anxiety. Some worry it will make people lazy, but that's not supported by evidence. People want purpose and contribution, not just money. What UBI does is give them the freedom to pursue education, care for family, or start businesses without desperation. The real question isn't whether we can afford UBI—it's whether we can afford not to implement it. Rising inequality and automation are creating unprecedented challenges.
